result:
I'll draft Batch 7 as an IPv6-disable script from the handoff and CIS results, and I'll only read Johnny and the repo before writing the plan and script.The CSV treats 3.1.1 as a manual IPv6-off check and 3.3.2.1–.8 as N/A once that is true. I’ll read Johnny’s listeners and sysctl before writing the script.CIS treats IPv6 as off when `disable_ipv6=1` is set on `all` and `default`. `0.0.0.0:22` is a separate socket from `[::]:22`, so this batch can do that with sysctl and skip GRUB.The sysctl append path can write the keys twice. I’ll collapse that into one edit before the script is reviewable.Batch 7 is drafted and has not been run. It turns IPv6 off with sysctl only. There is no GRUB change, no `ipv6.disable=1`, and no reboot.

## Detail

`docs/cis-fix/batch-7.md` and `docs/cis-fix/batch-7.sh` are the draft. Scope is CIS 3.1.1 plus 3.3.2.1–3.3.2.8. The local audit in `docs/cis-local/cis-3-audit.sh` prints "IPv6 is not enabled" when `net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6` and `net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6` are both `1`. That is the method this batch uses. `ipv6.disable=1` is the other way that script accepts, and it needs a cmdline change and a reboot. This batch does not do that.

Read-only SSH on 2026-11-04, no sudo: `eno3` is `192.168.50.152/24`, default route via `eno3`, three SSH sessions from `192.168.50.223`. `ss` shows TCP `0.0.0.0:22` and `[::]:22`. `ssh.socket` has both `ListenStream` lines and `BindIPv6Only=ipv6-only`, so the IPv4 socket does not depend on the IPv6 one. The only other IPv6 listener is chrony on `[::1]:323`, next to `127.0.0.1:323`. `disable_ipv6` is `0` on every interface. No IPv6 default route. `/etc/ufw/ufw.conf` is `ENABLED=yes` and `/etc/default/ufw` is `IPV6=yes`. This batch does not reload ufw and does not set `IPV6=no`. **[Assumption]** that combination leaves the existing IPv4 SSH sockets up. PASTE 1 checks the address and `0.0.0.0:22` after the sysctl write and puts both keys back to `0` if either check fails.

How AJ runs it:

```bash
scp docs/cis-fix/batch-7.sh aj@192.168.50.152:cis-audit/batch-7.sh
```

From an SSH session on Johnny, with a second SSH session from `192.168.50.0/24` already open:

```bash
sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-7.sh
```

That is PASTE 1. It backs up `/etc/sysctl.d/60-johnny-cis-network.conf` to `/root/60-johnny-cis-network.conf.pre-batch7`, appends the two `disable_ipv6 = 1` lines, and applies them with `sysctl -w` only. It also writes `/etc/systemd/system/ssh.socket.d/60-johnny-cis-ipv4.conf` so a later boot listens on `0.0.0.0:22` only, then `systemctl daemon-reload`. It does not restart `ssh.socket`. The live `[::]:22` socket stays until that unit is restarted. Do not restart it in this batch. The sysctl change is immediate. The drop-in takes effect at the next boot, together with the sysctl file. No reboot is required for 3.1.1.

PASTE 2 is console-only, and only if IPv4 SSH is already dead: `sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-7.sh 2`. Full undo while SSH still works is `## Rollback` in `docs/cis-fix/batch-7.md`.

`bash -n` on the script succeeded. Nothing was written to Johnny. The CSV and the handoff were not touched.

## Relay

Batch 7 draft is `docs/cis-fix/batch-7.md` and `docs/cis-fix/batch-7.sh`. IPv6 off by `disable_ipv6=1` on `all` and `default` in `60-johnny-cis-network.conf`. No `ipv6.disable=1`, no GRUB, no reboot. Live check: `0.0.0.0:22` is its own `ssh.socket` listener (`BindIPv6Only=ipv6-only`); `[::]:22` and chrony `[::1]:323` have IPv4 twins. Script refuses other listeners, requires `192.168.50.152/24` on `eno3` and a LAN SSH peer, writes an ssh.socket drop-in without restarting the socket, `sysctl -w` only those two keys, and reverts them if v4 SSH disappears. ufw is `ENABLED=yes` / `IPV6=yes` and is not reloaded. PASTE 2 is `sudo bash ~/cis-audit/batch-7.sh 2` at KVM only. `bash -n` passed. Not run.

## Outline

- Scope: 3.1.1 and 3.3.2.1–3.3.2.8, sysctl method, no boot cmdline
- Live: IPv4 SSH on `eno3` is separate from `[::]:22`; no IPv6-only service that this batch needs
- PASTE 1: backup, drop-in without socket restart, `sysctl -w`, stop if `0.0.0.0:22` or `.152` is gone
- PASTE 2 and `## Rollback`: restore the sysctl backup and set the keys back to `0`
- Not done: reboot, ufw `IPV6=no`, CSV, handoff, anything on Johnny
